decision_rule: A later disclosure is not a separate event when it merely republishes the same underlying dataset. A distinct trial, indication, independently enrolled cohort with a different prespecified clinical question, or regulator milestone may be retained when the new information is independently valuation-relevant and first-public at the new event date.

groups.rationale: BrigHtn and HALO were separate randomized Phase 2 trials in resistant versus uncontrolled hypertension, with separately enrolled populations and separate first-public topline disclosures. HALO is not a conference repetition of BrigHtn data.

HARMONY is a separate F2-F3 pre-cirrhotic Phase 2b trial. SYMMETRY Cohort D is an independently enrolled expansion cohort of 31 patients already receiving GLP-1 therapy with T2D and F1-F3 fibrosis, with a 12-week primary safety/tolerability aim. The SYMMETRY main study is a separately randomized 182-patient compensated-cirrhosis F4 study with a 36-week histologic primary endpoint. Cohort D and the main study therefore answer different prespecified clinical questions in different patient cohorts and are not duplicate releases of one dataset.

MIRA and ARGO are separate randomized Phase 2 trials of sonelokimab in hidradenitis suppurativa and active psoriatic arthritis respectively. They are separate indications, patient populations, protocols and first-public datasets.

ENTRIGUE and ENLIVEN are separate Phase 2 programs of pegozafermin in severe hypertriglyceridemia and NASH, with separate protocols and datasets. ENTRIGUE is not excluded as a duplicate; it is excluded separately by the frozen liquidity floor.
